relevance_note: First description of heterozygous germline TNFAIP3 loss-of-function mutations in patients: 'high penetrance heterozygous germline mutations in the NFκB regulatory protein TNFAIP3 (A20) in six unrelated families'.
method_note: Read the full Markdown manually and assembled the JSON with a short Python script in the scratch directory; Table 1 (families as rows) values were typed by hand from the table and checked against it cell by cell, and every span was checked verbatim by script. Per-patient clinical data are in Supplementary Table 1, which is not in the Markdown, so individual-level phenotypes are sparse. Labels: the paper uses P4, P5, P6 (and P9) but does not label Family 1, 3, 4, 5 or 6 members in the text, so labels such as 'Family 1 affected daughter 1' and 'Family 3 patient' are descriptive constructions (daughter numbering is arbitrary); 'Patient 6' (Discussion, Fig. 5c) is treated as P6. Families 3, 4 and 5 are each represented by one patient (the screened carrier) because the number of affected members is not given. Family 6 members (the Behçet's cohort patient and her two affected daughters) are linked to Table 1 'Family 6' by the identical protein change p.Pro268Leufs*19. Not given rows: patient P9 (mentioned only in Fig. 2d; family and variant not stated, likely one of the Family 3-6 patients); the Family 1 maternal unaffected relatives and the three unaffected Family 2 members (tested only as unlabeled groups; their genotypes are implied by segregation but not stated). The Family 1 TNFRSF9 candidate variant is not recorded (no variant description; attributed to the family, not one person). Family 1's features ('early-onset systemic inflammation, arthralgia/arthritis, oral/genital ulcers and ocular inflammation') are stated for the family's disorder, not per person, so they were not assigned to the three individuals. 'oral/genital ulcers' for P4/P5/P6 was read as both oral and genital ulcers. Elevated inflammatory markers for P6 is inferred from 'anakinra normalized markers of systemic inflammation'. Group exclusions: 'overt autoimmune disease was only diagnosed in Patient 6' and 'none of our patients have developed lymphomas or other malignancies' applied to all 12 study patients (not to P6's untested sister); they were not propagated to specific checklist items (e.g. autoimmune thyroiditis). Variant class: authors describe their variants collectively as 'nonsense and frameshift variants'; the class per variant was assigned from that statement plus the printed notation (* vs fs); only Family 6 is explicitly called frameshift. Inheritance left 'not reported' for all: Table 1 lists Family 4 as 'De novo' without describing parental testing, and parent-to-child transmission in Families 1, 2 and 6 is implied but not stated. Inconsistencies in the paper: Family 1 ancestry 'Caucasian' (text) vs 'European Canadian' (Table 1); Family 2 'Italian ancestry' (text) vs 'European American' (Table 1), both recorded; Family 2 protein printed 'p.Phe224Serfs*4' (text) vs 'p. Phe224Serfs*4' (Table 1, with a space); Abstract says six families while Fig. 1a shows 'Pedigrees of 5 families'; Methods list 7+4+2 evaluated patients but no total of mutation-positive patients is stated, so n_patients_reported is null. Genomic coordinates are printed without a genome build.
